summary: The comment argues against limiting or eliminating E‑Rate, against restricting consultant fee structures, against federal control of classroom technology use, calls for a longer comment period, and opposes additional administrative burdens that would hinder participation. The commenter opposes any termination or restriction of the E‑Rate program, rejects limits on consultant compensation, and objects to federal screen‑time or instructional technology limits, while urging that new administrative requirements be scalable and not create barriers to participation.
